unit.title: Cooperation and Caring for Each Other

contentBlocks.text: Have you ever worked together with someone to build something, clean up, or finish a game? That's cooperation — and it's how communities really get things done.

Cooperation means working together toward a shared goal — like a group of friends building a tower of blocks together, or a whole class cleaning up the classroom together. Cooperation usually works better than trying to do a big job all alone. Think of a time you cooperated with someone else to get something done, and describe what happened.
You now understand cooperation — working together toward a shared goal. This week we'll explore more ways communities cooperate and care for each other.

objectives: Explain in simple words that cooperation means working together toward a shared goal
Describe a real personal experience of cooperating with someone else
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's community-helper content.
2. Introduce cooperation using the block-building or classroom-cleanup example.
3. Discuss why cooperation often works better than doing a big job alone.
4. Have the child describe a real time they cooperated with someone.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Close by planning one small cooperative task to do together this week.
differentiationTips: Struggling: act out a simple cooperative task together in the moment (like tidying up) rather than only discussing a past example
Ready for more: ask the child to think of a job that would be very hard for just one person, and explain why cooperation helps
This is the first lesson of a new unit — a good moment to connect it back to last week's community-helper theme
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a discussion and drawing activity — check that the child can explain cooperation as working together toward a shared goal, with a real personal example.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's 'cooperation' description, introducing a genuine civics/social skill that builds on last week's community-helper foundation.
